claims.text: The initial titanium- and nickel-containing high-entropy alloy is a single-phase solid solution with standard impurity levels.
Vacuum arc remelting, high-purity raw materials, and inert or high-vacuum processing can reduce contaminant levels in the alloy.
Contaminants can act as nucleation sites for phase segregation.
High operating temperatures and aggressive atmospheres promote phase instabilities in the target alloy.
Preventing impurity-induced secondary-phase formation maintains the stability of the single-phase solid solution.
Reducing impurity levels diminishes heterogeneous nucleation during thermal aging.
Diminished heterogeneous nucleation limits phase segregation during thermal aging.
Phase segregation can reduce high-temperature creep resistance.
Phase segregation can reduce high-temperature tensile strength.
Enhanced impurity control will produce higher elevated-temperature tensile strength than conventional processing of the same alloy.
Enhanced impurity control will improve elevated-temperature creep resistance relative to conventional processing of the same alloy.
The magnitude of mechanical-property enhancement and long-term phase stability may depend on impurity type and concentration.
